about: Meson option sets of the lab's Mesa builds, copied from the 'Build Options:' line of each recorded build's meson-logs/meson-log.txt, in that order. 'glslang' says whether the recorded build had glslangValidator on PATH ('required' by the configuration, 'on-path', 'not-on-path'). build-mesa.ps1 passes them verbatim and fails if the new log's line differs. docs/build.md quotes them; change both together. 'ships' names, per target, the file names the release ships that target as: the build writes one copy per name next to the target and stamps each with its own version resource (BD-166, tools/build/versionstamp.py), because the resource names the file it belongs to and one Mesa vulkan_radeon.dll ships both as vulkan_radeon.dll and as amdgpu_wddm_radv.dll. A target that no release ships has no entry and is not stamped. 'compilers' and 'variants' add to a set and leave it as recorded (Add-MesonVariants, tools/build/common.ps1): build-mesa.ps1 -Compiler adds the arguments of the compiler's entry to every set, and -Variant adds the named variants, each with its options for every compiler and under a compiler's name for that compiler only. An option of a variant replaces the set's option of the same name in its place; default_options apply only where the set has no option of that name; c_args go at the end of -Dc_args and -Dcpp_args, link_args at the end of -Dc_link_args and -Dcpp_link_args. No shipped build uses a variant.

msvc.description: cl.exe, link.exe and lib.exe of the Visual Studio developer environment: the compiler of every recorded and shipped set

clang-cl.description: clang-cl.exe, lld-link.exe and llvm-lib.exe of an LLVM Windows toolchain (build-mesa.ps1 -ClangToolchain, default LLVM 23.1.4), in the same Visual Studio environment for headers, libraries and rc.exe. /clang:-ffp-contract=off: a multiply and an add round separately, as with MSVC, whose /fp:precise does not contract them; with FMA in the instruction set (variant isa), clang would fuse them into one FMA, which rounds once, and NIR constant folding could then give other values than the MSVC build. -gline-tables-only: the PDB has functions and lines but no types. With full CodeView types, LLVM 23.1.2 and 23.1.4 write a self-referencing LF_FIELDLIST for an enum whose field list needs a continuation record (VkStructureType) when ThinLTO import puts a second copy of the enum into a module, and the PDB step of lld-link then does not end (docs/build.md)

release.description: meson buildtype release with the PDB: optimisation level 3, /O2 /Gw, in place of the /O2 of debugoptimized. A set without b_ndebug gets -Db_ndebug=false, the NDEBUG state that debugoptimized gave it: in a release buildtype, meson's default b_ndebug=if-release defines NDEBUG

lto.description: whole-program optimisation of each target over the Mesa objects and static libraries it links: /GL and /LTCG with MSVC, ThinLTO in lld-link with clang-cl. Without -Dallow-broken-lto=true, Mesa's meson.build refuses b_lto; the option also appends -lto to the Mesa version string

isa.description: the x86-64-v3 instruction set, the CPU requirement of the project (owner, 2026-10-21): /arch:AVX2 with MSVC; with clang-cl, -march=x86-64-v3 (AVX, AVX2, BMI1, BMI2, F16C, FMA, LZCNT, MOVBE), tuned for Zen 2. Never -march=znver2 or -march=native: znver2 adds SSE4a, which Intel CPUs do not have, and native is the CPU of the build machine

radv.description: RADV Vulkan ICD with the WDDM2 winsys, ACO only (no LLVM)

radv-mt.description: RADV Vulkan ICD with the WDDM2 winsys, ACO only (no LLVM), static C runtime (the radv set plus -Db_vscrt=mt): the ICD runs inside every game, and a game that ships an older msvcp140.dll beside its exe hands it to every DLL that imports MSVCP140.dll by name
radv-mt.recorded_script: none yet: the radv set plus -Db_vscrt=mt, first built 2026-10-01

radv-system.description: RADV Vulkan ICD for the x64 system loader (payload/vulkan/vulkan_radeon.dll): the radv-mt options, with static C runtime and NDEBUG in both flavours. The Mesa source must carry the CRT link-selection fix and the NDEBUG build fix a7f44c96. This recipe name stays because the release scripts and build records name the x64 system slot by it (BD-178)
radv-system.recorded_script: BD-178: the radv-mt option set under the existing x64 system-slot recipe name

llvmpipe-umd.description: Desktop D3D10 UMD: Gallium d3d10umd frontend on llvmpipe/softpipe, statically linked LLVM, static CRT

zink-umd.description: Native D3D10 UMD: Gallium d3d10umd frontend on Zink over the Vulkan ICD, no LLVM

zink-gl.description: OpenGL through Zink (WGL): app-local opengl32.dll plus libgallium_wgl.dll, no LLVM

zink-gl-icd.description: System OpenGL ICD on Zink (WGL): the gallium wgl target DLL renamed amdgpu_wddm_gl.dll, which the display adapter's driver key names in OpenGLDriverName and OpenGLDriverNameWow, no LLVM. The zink-gl set plus -Db_ndebug=true (no live assert in a DLL that loads into every OpenGL application), -Db_vscrt=mt (the same reason the radv-mt set takes it: an application that ships its own msvcp140.dll hands it to every DLL that imports that name) and -Dgallium-wgl-dll-name=amdgpu_wddm_gl. buildtype stays debugoptimized, as in every shipped Mesa component of this project: /O2 with NDEBUG and a PDB
zink-gl-icd.recorded_script: none yet: first built 2026-10-12 for BD-076, x64 and x86 (scratch/bd076-gl/out/BUILD.md)
